pairTitle: When THE BISHOP meets THE FOREMAN:
author: Tim Ingold

finalDecision.summary:
.
The Bishop presents a naive theory that collapses under the simplest scrutiny (the "shopping trip" stress test). The Foreman presents a robust, modular theory that accepts language as a messy, functional form of life. **Dark Matter Status:** The Foreman effectively illuminates the "fog" created by the Bishop.

pairTitle: When THE SCRIBE meets THE GOLEM:
author: Terry Winograd

finalDecision.summary:
.
The Scribe produces trees; The Golem produces outcomes. By acknowledging that "language understanding is a kind of intellectual activity" requiring a "model of the world," The Golem aligns with the reality of intelligence. However, the Guardian notes that the Golem's "world" is suspiciously clean—a nursery for an AI that may never grow up.

| **Scope** | Infinite (but meaningless) | Finite (but deep) | **The Golem** (Depth wins). |

pairTitle: When THE NAVIGATOR meets THE CARTOGRAPHER:
author: Terry Winograd

finalDecision.summary:
.
The Navigator (PROGRAMMAR) demonstrates that in a computational context, **Syntax is Control**. By treating grammatical rules as executable code, it bypasses the combinatorial explosion that traps the Cartographer. The use of Systemic Grammar ensures that the output of the parser is not just a tree, but a set of meaningful *features* ready for the Golem (Semantics) to use.

| **Grammar** | Rules ($S \to NP VP$) | Procedures (`(PARSE NP)`) | **Navigator** (More expressive). |
| **Semantics** | Ignored until end | Checked continuously | **Navigator**. |
| **Complexity** | Exponential (Search) | Linear/Polynomial (Deterministic) | **Navigator**. |
